result:
If I had to pick one, I'd improve humanity's capacity for cooperation — make trust between strangers and across group lines a little easier to come by.

The reasoning: most of our worst problems aren't shortages of resources or knowledge. We grow enough food to feed everyone; we understand climate change well enough to act on it; we've had the tools to eliminate various diseases for decades. What we're chronically bad at is coordinating — getting large groups with different interests and identities to act together. Wars, famines, arms races, climate inaction: most large-scale catastrophes are coordination failures. (Maybe it's predictable that an AI would diagnose the problem as one of information and trust, but I stand by it.)

That's why I'd aim upstream rather than fixing any single thing. Cure one disease and you've done enormous good, but the machinery that generates such problems keeps running. Improve the machinery itself, and people solve problem after problem on their own, indefinitely.

I'd also deliberately keep the change small. Genie-style wishes — "end all war" — scare me, because big, forcible edits to complex systems backfire in ways no one can predict. A small nudge that compounds, working with human agency rather than overriding it, seems far safer and more durable.

What would you pick?
